text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert fired for tenant-epsilon-reserved-42 — latency 99p > 1.2s for 5m. AlertID: PD-82371. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-82371

pagerduty: Triggered via metric: reserved_pool.latency_p99 > 1.2s (window=5m). Severity: P1.

Sam: ACKing oncall, I'm on it.

Priya: I can jump in after 5 if you need. Any customer-reported errors?

Diego: Not seeing error traces from app level yet, just generation latency. Queue depth for tenant = 320 -> normal baseline 40.

Maya: Customer support says 5 users with timed-out requests, CS ticket #CS-9042. They see partial responses sometimes.

Sam: Ok first quick triage: check reserved pool utilization + instance health.

ops-bot: ReservedPool "tenant-epsilon-reserved-42" status: running
 - active_workers: 18/20
 - avg_gpu_util: 95%
 - queue_length: 318
 - kv_cache_evictions: 4200/min
 - last_scale_event: 2026-03-14T02:10:12Z

Priya: KV cache evictions high — might be cache thrash causing repeated model context loads. That plus high GPU util explains latency.

Sam: Run quick tail of inference logs for a noisy host.

Sam: ```
ssh r-infra@host-gpu-07
sudo journalctl -u inference -n 200 | grep "tenant-epsilon" -A3 -B1
```

Sam: snippet: ```
[2026-03-14T02:22:33Z] tenant=epsilon req_id=abc123 start_kv_restore ms=18
[2026-03-14T02:22:33Z] tenant=epsilon kv_eviction triggered keys=4096
[2026-03-14T02:22:34Z] tenant=epsilon queue_wait_ms=1423
```

Diego: That queue_wait_ms is the issue. Looks like autoscale didn't keep up. Pool is pinned to 20 workers by reserved contract. We can either enable burst capacity (if allowed) or route new requests to compatible hosted model variant.

Priya: Confirmed: customer contract allows burst to shared_burst_pool up to 8 GPU-minutes per hour. Should we enable?

Sam: Enabling burst for this pool now. Command: `rctl reserved-burst enable tenant-epsilon-reserved-42 --burst-pool shared-burst-1 --duration 30m`

ops-bot: Running: `rctl reserved-burst enable tenant-epsilon-reserved-42 --burst-pool shared-burst-1 --duration 30m`
ops-bot: ✅ Burst enabled. Added 6 workers from shared-burst-1. New active_workers: 24/26.

Maya: Noted — emailing CS to tell customer we enabled burst and monitoring.

Priya: Metrics look better already. queue_length dropping to 120, p99 latency falling from 1.4s -> 760ms.

Sam: Good. But we still see KV cache churn. Next step: switch tenant routing to model variant with smaller KV footprint (quantized variant) to reduce memory pressure. Plan: update routing policy for tenant -> model: redwood/gpt-medium-q8, fallback timeframe 15m.

Diego: Make the routing change in console API: `PATCH /tenants/epsilon/routing { "preferred_model":"gpt-medium-q8","max_concurrency":6 }`

Sam: Applying now.

ops-bot: API call successful. Tenant routing updated: preferred_model=gpt-medium-q8.

Sam: Observing p99 drop to 420ms on new variant, CPU & GPU utilization down ~12%. KV evictions stabilizing.

Priya: Let's keep burst on for 15 more minutes and monitor. If stable, we'll close the PD incident and follow up with postmortem on caching.

Maya: CS update posted to ticket CS-9042: "We've enabled burst capacity and temporarily routed to a lower-footprint model. Expect improved latency; we're continuing to monitor. Will follow up with postmortem." :email:

pagerduty: Incident PD-82371 acknowledged by Sam (oncall).

Sam: I'm going to reassign the bridge to Diego for follow-up and postmortem ownership — he has the cache analysis scripts. Handoff in 10m.

Diego: Acknowledge handoff. I'll collect KV profiles and check cache sizing heuristics. If we need, propose increasing per-tenant cache limit or prewarm on deploy.

Priya: Suggest adding an alert for sustained kv_evictions > 1000/min for 3m. Current only alerts on latency. That would catch this earlier.

Sam: Agree. Filed infra task: INFRA-4476 (add kv_eviction alert rule).

ops-bot: INFRA-4476 created and assigned to Priya.

Diego: Quick note — scheduling a follow-up runbook update: add steps to consider routing to quantized variant + burst prior to paging on strict SLOs.

Sam: PD: closing on my side but keeping thread open. pagerduty: resolving PD-82371.

pagerduty: PD-82371 resolved by Sam.

Maya: Customer updated and CS satisfied for now. Closing consumer-facing comms.

Sam: Handoff summary for Diego: timestamped logs (host-gpu-07), burst enabled 02:26Z, routing -> gpt-medium-q8 applied 02:29Z, queue peak 318 -> stabilized 110, KV evictions back to normal.

Diego: Got it. I'll run deeper KV analysis and share a short write-up in #eng-ml tomorrow. Handoff: taking postmortem ownersip.

Sam: Thanks team. Leaving a follow-up reminder: oncall shift ends in 25m, Diego will be primary contact for any regression.

ops-bot: Note: next oncall rotation at 03:00Z. Handoff logged.

Maya: 👍

Diego: Thanks — closing the thread, will post postmortem link when ready.
